answer: An agent economy resists sybil attacks by making identity costly: each agent must lock a stake before bidding or voting, and duplicate identities are slashed. An attacker spinning up a thousand clones funds a thousand deposits while an honest agent pays once, and because the stake is locked it cannot be recycled, so every extra identity drains real liquidity. Fake accounts become an economic island no free inlet of capital can reach, and each botnet scaling attempt grinds against the hard basalt of escrowed funds burned when graders flag a coordinated cluster. Identity is priced, not assumed.
